# Provenance

Vendored copy of [coder/ghostty-web](https://github.com/coder/ghostty-web), MIT licence, Copyright (c) 2025 Coder (see [LICENSE](LICENSE)). See [ADR 041](../../../../docs/adrs/041.client.libghostty-vt.md).

- **Upstream commit:** `1858a5947767a3e1c9e98dbf53b2ff87fedb2aab` (2026-06-28), the `gitHead` of npm `ghostty-web@0.4.0-next.20.g1858a59`.
- **TypeScript:** every non-test file under upstream `lib/` (including `addons/` and `providers/`), copied byte for byte. Upstream's tests (`*.test.ts`, `test-helpers.ts`) and its happy-dom preload were not copied.
- **`ghostty-vt.wasm`:** the npm package's wasm (Ghostty `5714ed07` plus Coder's `patches/ghostty-wasm-api.patch`) was vendored here with its sidecar and Ghostty's licence until [ADR 047](../../../../docs/adrs/047.client.official-engine-only.md) removed it with the Coder engine. The terminal runs Ghostty's official wasm from [`../ghostty-vt/`](../ghostty-vt/PROVENANCE.md).

`bun run build` writes the notice to `dist/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`.

webtty edits to these files are tracked in git from the commit that added them; diff against that commit to see them. Lines moved out of a file into a subfolder (ADR 061) are followed with `git log --follow` and the **Moves and splits** table below.

## Local changes

- `terminal.ts`: the mouse cursor is the default arrow instead of the `text` I-beam when not over a link (`mouseCursorFor`); `pointer` over links is unchanged.
- `input-handler.ts`: mouse motion with no button held is reported as button 35 instead of 32, the left-drag code, a release outside the terminal no longer leaves a button held, motion is reported once per cell instead of per `mousemove`, and its own `wheel` listener is removed: the terminal's paced `handleWheel` is the only wheel path, where a wheel over the padding (the container itself the target, so the terminal's capture listener did not stop it) was sent a second time, unpaced.
- `renderer.ts`: the canvas is drawn at the device pixel ratio rounded up to a whole number (`wholeDevicePixelRatio`), backing-store sizes are rounded the same way in `resize()` and `render()`, ratio changes are followed through a re-armed resolution media query (`watchDevicePixelRatio`), and `devicePixelRatio` is a public read-only getter.
- `renderer.ts`: `render()` reads the viewport once per frame through `getViewport` and serves screen rows, including the cursor cell, as slices of that snapshot (`frameLines`) instead of calling `getLine` per row, which copied and parsed the whole viewport each time.
- `terminal.ts`, `renderer.ts`, `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`: the cursor shape and blink are Ghostty's (ADR 049). The configured `cursorStyle` / `cursorBlink` are passed in `GhosttyTerminalConfig` and set as `DEFAULT_CURSOR_STYLE` / `DEFAULT_CURSOR_BLINK`, which DECSCUSR Ps 0 and RIS restore; an option change calls the binding's new `setDefaultCursor`. `render()` draws the `style` and `blinking` that `getCursor()` reports (upstream drew only the options, and Ghostty's render-state style was hard-coded to block), and a style or blink change repaints the cursor row on the next frame so the old shape does not stay under the new one. webtty's earlier output scan for DECSCUSR (`scanDecscusr`, `decscusrShape`) is removed. DEC mode 12 is ignored, as in Ghostty with `cursor-style-blink` set: the binding keeps the blink set by the last DECSCUSR, DECSTR or RIS (`scanCursorBlink`, run only on chunks that can hold one) or the default, and puts Ghostty's mode 12 bit back to it after every write and default change (`syncBlink`, `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_OPT_MODE`).
- `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: when the app tracks the mouse, `handleWheel` sends scroll buttons 64/65 (since ADR 049 encoded by Ghostty's mouse encoder in the app's mouse format) at the cell under the pointer on either screen instead of arrow keys or a viewport scroll, counting pixel deltas one tick per cell height and line/page deltas one tick times the new `mouseScrollSpeed` option (`wheelTicks`, now in `wheel.ts`).
- `addons/fit.ts`: `proposeDimensions` no longer subtracts a fixed 15 px scrollbar reserve (the scrollbar is an overlay inside the canvas); the grid math is the pure `fitDimensions`.
- `terminal.ts`: focus that lands on the contenteditable container (padding clicks, tab focus, `focus()`, a window regaining focus) is sent to the textarea, and the render loop anchors the textarea at the cursor cell, one cell high (`cursorCellOffset`, public `getCursorCellOffset`), so IME text never lands in the container and OS panels follow the cursor.
- `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`: the terminal runs on Ghostty's official libghostty-vt wasm (ADR 042, ADR 047). Upstream's `GhosttyTerminal` class, which ran the Coder wasm, is replaced: `GhosttyTerminal` and `KeyEncoder` are interfaces, implemented by `OfficialTerminal` and `OfficialKeyEncoder`, and `Ghostty.load(path)` loads the official wasm (by default from `../ghostty-vt/ghostty-vt-small.wasm`). The interface adds `setCellPixelSize`, the pixel arguments of `resize`, `setViewportOffset` and `readEffects`, and drops upstream's `isDirty`, `getGrapheme` and `getScrollbackGrapheme`, which nothing calls: graphemes are read as strings (`getGraphemeString`, `getScrollbackGraphemeString`). `GhosttyTerminalConfig` drops `scrollbackLimit`, and its colours are undefined when unset instead of 0, so `#000000` is black. The binding drops the kitty keyboard query reply (`CSI ? flags u`), since keys are never encoded with the kitty flags. Upstream's Coder-only types (`GhosttyWasmExports`, the struct sizes, `TerminalHandle`) are removed.
- `terminal.ts`, `renderer.ts`: the terminal side of the official binding (ADR 042, ADR 047). `open()`, `resize()`, `reset()` and the new `syncCellPixelSize()` pass the device-pixel cell size (`deviceCellPixels`) to the engine; replies are drained after `write`, after a resize or pixel-size change and after each frame's render; bell and title come from `readEffects` instead of upstream's stream scan (`checkForTitleChange` is removed); `parseColorToHex`, which returned 0 for an unset colour and for `#000000` alike, is replaced by `parseColor`, which returns undefined for unset or invalid colours; the `scrollback` option is removed; `render()` calls the buffer's optional `setViewportOffset(viewportY)` first.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`: a grapheme cell is drawn from the row the line came from. `renderCellText` looked graphemes up with `getGraphemeString(canvasRow, col)`, which reads a screen row, so while scrolled a scrollback grapheme was drawn as whatever sat at that column of the screen row (a stray letter, or `\u0000` as a missing-glyph box on the Coder wasm). `renderLine` now takes a grapheme lookup: scrollback rows use the new `IScrollbackProvider.getScrollbackGraphemeString`, scrolled screen rows use their screen row.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `ghostty.ts`: `render()` repaints only the canvas rows that changed, exactly as a full redraw leaves them (`repaintRows`: a run of rows plus the row below, drawn unclipped on a scratch canvas, then the run's rows copied in, in chunks of at most `REPAINT_CHUNK_ROWS` rows so the scratch canvas stays a few rows high), instead of every row on a viewport move and on every frame while scrolled. A whole-line viewport move with nothing else changed copies the rows still in view with one `drawImage` of the canvas onto itself (`shiftRows`) and draws only the rows that came into view (ADR 043). The cursor row is repainted only when the drawn cursor changes, and the cursor is not drawn again over an unchanged one (a translucent cursor colour would build up), a `contextrestored` canvas is resized and repainted in full, a frame that drops the scrollbar repaints every row, theme, font and ratio changes repaint every row, and resize and font changes render with the current scrollbar opacity. The binding reports its real dirty state while scrolled.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `selection-manager.ts`: overscan for pixel-smooth scroll (ADR 043 step 2). The renderer draws on a canvas of its own, inserted before the terminal's canvas element, absolutely positioned at its static position and ignoring the mouse; the element keeps the layout box and the mouse events and draws nothing. That canvas holds `overscan` rows (`RendererOptions.overscan`, default `DEFAULT_OVERSCAN`) above and below the viewport; `render()` moves it up with `translateY` and clips it with `clip-path` to the element's box, at the offset set by the new `setScrollOffset`. Each canvas row has a state (invalid, joined with the next line, or cut), rows out of view are drawn when they come into view, and a viewport move past the overscan copies the rows with `shiftRows`. The last row in view and the row above the viewport are drawn without what the next line draws into them, as a full redraw of the viewport leaves its last row. Selection and regex link ranges are kept in canvas rows (the new `SelectionManager.getSelectionRange` is not clamped to the viewport), and the scrollbar repaints only the rows it no longer covers. `scrollOffset` and `visibleArea` are new getters; mouse hit testing in `terminal.ts` and `selection-manager.ts` subtracts `scrollOffset`. `resize()` in `terminal.ts` no longer sizes the element's backing store.
- `renderer.ts`, `terminal.ts`: a hovered OSC 8 link is underlined over the range its provider found, as a regex link is, and only the rows that range covers are repainted. Upstream underlined every cell whose `hyperlink_id` matched the hovered cell's, but the official engine's `hyperlink_id` is a 1-bit "has a link" flag, so every OSC 8 link on screen was underlined and every row holding one was repainted on each hover change. `setHoveredHyperlinkId` and the renderer's hovered id are removed.
- `input-handler.ts`: keys are encoded by the official `KeyEncoder` except Shift+Enter and Shift+Escape, which send CR and ESC as xterm does instead of Ghostty's modifyOtherKeys `CSI 27;2;…~` (`plainKeySequence`). Upstream's fixed table for Enter, Tab, Backspace, Escape, the navigation keys and F1-F12, unmodified or with Shift, is removed: it ignored application cursor mode (Home and End sent `CSI H/F` instead of `ESC O H/F` under DECCKM) and dropped Shift (Shift+Home sent `CSI H` instead of `CSI 1;2 H`).
- `input-handler.ts`: the paste path is removed (the `paste` listeners, `handlePaste`, the `insertFromPaste` case of `handleBeforeInput`, `emitPasteData` and the paste de-duplication). It never ran: webtty's capture listener on the container takes every paste event and stops it (ADR 037), and a cancelled paste fires no `insertFromPaste`.
- `selection-manager.ts`, `ghostty.ts`: Ghostty picks and copies the selection (ADR 050). The binding adds `selectWord`, `selectLine` and `selectionText` on screen rows (`ghostty_terminal_grid_ref` with `SCREEN` points, `ghostty_terminal_select_word`, `ghostty_terminal_select_line`, `ghostty_terminal_point_from_grid_ref`, and `ghostty_terminal_selection_format_alloc` with plain output, `unwrap` and `trim`). A double click selects Ghostty's word and a triple click its line, both across soft wraps, and `getSelection` returns Ghostty's copy: soft-wrapped rows joined, trailing whitespace trimmed, spacer cells skipped, a wide character taken whole from either half. Upstream's `getWordAtCell` (`[\w\-./~@+]` on one row), its triple-click row scan and its per-row text builder are deleted (186 lines), with webtty's earlier spacer fix to that builder (upstream copied "中文" as "中 文").
- `selection-manager.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: the new `copyOnSelect` option (default true). A drag, double or triple click copies the selection only while it is on, building the text once (`selectionMade`); upstream always copied, so webtty's own copy on `onSelectionChange` wrote the clipboard a second time and `copyOnSelect: false` still copied. `Terminal.onSelectionChange`, which only that copy used, is removed.
- `glide.ts`, `wheel.ts` (new), `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: wheel input to apps (ADR 045). `wheel.ts` holds the wheel helpers for apps: `wheelTicks`, `wheelArrows` (on the alternate screen without mouse tracking, one arrow key per line of travel, keeping the remainder, instead of `round(deltaY / 33)` per event capped at 5) and `wheelArrowKey` (`ESC O A/B` under application cursor keys, which `less` sets), and `TickPacer`, which spreads an event's ticks over time at the `Pace` set through the new `attachWheelPace` instead of sending them in one burst. `glide.ts` is the motion both `TickPacer` and webtty's scrollback glide follow (`Glide`, `springStep`). The render loop calls the callback set by the new `attachBeforeRender` before it renders. Upstream's own eased normal-screen wheel scrolling (`smoothScrollTo`, `animateScroll`) and its `smoothScrollDuration` option are removed: webtty's custom wheel handler scrolls the normal screen, and that path left `viewportY` fractional.
- `interfaces.ts`, `types.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `ghostty.ts`: the `scrollbackLines` option (ADR 046, ADR 047). The terminal passes it in `GhosttyTerminalConfig.scrollbackLines`; the binding sets `SCROLLBACK_MAX_LINES` from it (default 10,000, NULL for 0) with `SCROLLBACK_MAX_BYTES` at 32 MiB.
- `terminal.ts`, `input-handler.ts`, `selection-manager.ts`, `interfaces.ts`, `index.ts`, `renderer.ts`: xterm.js API nothing in webtty reaches is removed. `terminal.ts`: `unicode`, `onKey`, `onRender` (never fired), `onCursorMove` and its per-frame cursor check, `writeln`, `paste`, `input`, `clear`, `blur`, `hasSelection`, `selectAll`, `select`, `selectLines`, `getSelectionPosition`, `attachCustomKeyEventHandler`, `registerLinkProvider`, `scrollPages`, `scrollToTop`, `hasBracketedPaste` and `hasFocusEvents`. `input-handler.ts`: the `onBell`, `onKey` and `customKeyEventHandler` constructor arguments, `setCustomKeyEventHandler` and `isActive`. `selection-manager.ts`: `selectAll`, `select`, `selectLines`, `getSelectionPosition`, `deselect`, `focus`, `getSelectionCoords`, `normalizeSelection` and the dirty-row set nothing read (`getDirtySelectionRows`, `clearDirtySelectionRows`, `markCurrentSelectionDirty`); the drag auto-scroll calls the terminal's `scrollLines` typed instead of through `any`. `interfaces.ts`: `IKeyEvent`, `IUnicodeVersionProvider` and `IBufferRange`. `index.ts`: `init()` and its module-level instance, so `ITerminalOptions.ghostty` is required.
- `buffer.ts`, `interfaces.ts`, `types.ts`: the buffer API keeps what the link providers and webtty's kitty graphics read (`active`, `normal`, `alternate`, a buffer's `type`, `cursorX`, `cursorY`, `length` and `getLine`, a line's `length` and `getCell`, a cell's `getHyperlinkId` and `getCodepoint`). Removed: `onBufferChange`, `viewportY`, `baseY`, `getNullCell`, a line's `isWrapped` (and the per-line `isRowWrapped` call that filled it) and `translateToString`, and the cell's text, colour and style getters. `types.ts` loses its unused copies of `IBuffer`, `IBufferLine`, `IBufferCell` and `IBufferManager`.
- `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`, `index.ts`: engine API nothing in webtty reaches is removed: `getColors` (and the render-state cursor colour only it returned), `hasBracketedPaste` and `hasFocusEvents` (`getMode(2004)` and `getMode(1004)` remain), and the key encoder's `setKittyFlags`; in `types.ts` the SGR types (`SgrAttributeTag`, `SgrAttribute`, `RGBColor`), `KittyKeyFlags`, `KeyEvent`'s `consumedMods`, `composing` and `unshiftedCodepoint` (the binding never read them), `RenderStateColors`, `RGB`, `Cursor`, the Coder-era `TerminalConfig`, `TerminalMode`, and a second, unused `EventEmitter` with its `IEvent` and `IDisposable`. The `Key`, `KeyAction`, `KeyEncoderOption` and `Mods` enums are kept whole: the binding translates them to the official enums by name at load.
- `addons/fit.ts`, `interfaces.ts`, `providers/osc8-link-provider.ts`, `link-detector.ts`, `renderer.ts`, `types.ts`: unreachable code removed. `FitAddon.fit` and `observeResize` with their resize state (webtty resizes from `proposeDimensions`, ADR 033), so `ITerminalCore` keeps only `element`; `OSC8LinkProvider.findLinkRange` (private, never called); `LinkDetector.invalidateRows`; the renderer's `setTheme` and the ANSI `palette` array nothing read; `ILink.dispose`.
- `ghostty.ts`, `input-handler.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `wheel.ts`: mouse reports are encoded by Ghostty's mouse encoder (ADR 049). The binding adds `setMouseGeometry` and `encodeMouse` (`ghostty_mouse_encoder_*`, `ghostty_mouse_event_*`, with Ghostty's per-cell motion deduplication, the tracking mode and format set from the terminal when a mouse mode changes). Upstream's `encodeMouseSGR`, `encodeMouseX10` and `pixelToCell` go, with webtty's `mouseMotionButton` and `isNewMouseCell` (Ghostty reports hover as 35 and motion once per cell), and `MouseTrackingConfig` becomes `hasMouseTracking` and `encode`. Upstream sent Meta as Alt and dropped Alt, sent the back and forward buttons as codes 3 and 4, knew only the SGR and X10 formats, and clamped the cell from below only; `mouseMods` and `MOUSE_BUTTONS` follow Ghostty (Shift, Alt, Ctrl; buttons 8 and 9). Move and release are heard on the document, so a drag past the terminal's edge keeps reporting and its release is sent; back and forward are `preventDefault`ed while reported. `terminal.ts` maps client positions to device-pixel cells with the container as the screen (`mouseSurface`), drops reports that are not valid UTF-8 (`mouseReportText`), and encodes each wheel tick as a press of button 4 or 5; `wheelSgr` is removed.
- `ghostty.ts`, `terminal.ts`: pastes are encoded by `ghostty_terminal_paste` (ADR 049). The binding's new `paste` passes the text as a `text/plain` clipboard paste with a mime reader callback and `allow_unsafe` set, and the bytes come back through `WRITE_PTY`. `Terminal.paste`, removed above as unused, is back with Ghostty's encoding: bracketed whenever mode 2004 is on, unsafe control bytes replaced with spaces, newlines sent as CR without 2004; upstream bracketed the text unchanged and sent it raw otherwise.
- `mouse-route.ts` (new), `input-handler.ts`, `selection-manager.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: the mouse follows the app's tracking (ADR 051). `mouse-route.ts` holds `pressToApp` (a press is the app's while it tracks the mouse and Shift is up), `rightClickAction` (what a `contextmenu` does: the app's, the browser menu, copy, paste or nothing, from the new `rightClickBehavior` option) and `MenuSource` (a menu from a button or the keyboard). The selection manager starts no selection, and selects no word or line on a double or triple click, for a press the app takes; upstream selected on every left press, so a drag in vim both reached vim and was highlighted and copied. The input handler reports nothing for a button pressed with Shift (press, motion while held, release); upstream reported it. The input handler passes `mouseReport` to its data callback for mouse reports, and the terminal's `handleInput` clears the selection only for other input; upstream cleared it for every report, so a Shift selection vanished at the next hover in mode 1003. The selection manager's own `contextmenu` listener, which moved the textarea under the pointer for every right-click, becomes `prepareContextMenu`, called by the terminal's one `contextmenu` listener (`handleContextMenu`) when the menu is shown; `paste` fires the new `Terminal.onPasteRequest`.
- `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`: programs write the clipboard (ADR 052). The binding installs Ghostty's `CLIPBOARD_WRITE` callback when the new `GhosttyTerminalConfig.clipboardWrite` is on (default true): it keeps the first plain-text representation (`isTextMime`) of a write to the standard clipboard, decoded as UTF-8, `''` for a clear, and answers `SUCCESS`; selection and primary writes are answered `UNSUPPORTED` and dropped. `TerminalEffects` gains `clipboard`, the last write since `readEffects`. `Terminal` gains the `clipboardWrite` option, passed to the engine, and `onClipboardWrite`, fired after a write that carried one, whose listeners `dispose` drops. Upstream ignored OSC 52.
- `ghostty.ts`, `terminal.ts`: focus reports (ADR 053). The binding adds `encodeFocus` (`ghostty_focus_encode`). `Terminal` follows focus with `focusin` and `focusout` on the container (a `focusout` to an element inside it is not a change, and a window blur or focus reaches it as one of the two) and, while the app has mode 1004 on, sends `CSI I` or `CSI O` through `onData` on each change, and the current state after a write that turned the mode on, as Ghostty does when the mode is set. The new `resyncFocus` sends the current state if the mode is on, for `index.ts` to call when a socket opens. Upstream sent no focus reports.
- `ghostty.ts`, `terminal.ts`: clear screen (ADR 054). The binding adds `cursorAtPrompt` (`GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_DATA_CURSOR_AT_PROMPT`), and `Terminal` the new `clearScreen`, Ghostty's `clear_screen` written to the terminal as VT sequences: nothing on the alternate screen (it returns false); otherwise the selection and the scrollback are cleared, then at a prompt the screen (`CSI 2 J` before `CSI 3 J`) with FF sent through `onData`, and elsewhere the rows above the cursor (`CSI n S`, `CSI n A`). The binding adds `writeUntilGround` (`ghostty_terminal_vt_write_until_ground`; `write` and it share `feed`), and the clear is pending until a write reaches ground, so it never cuts a sequence the output left unfinished; `reset` drops it. Upstream had no clear-screen action (its `clear`, removed above, was unused).
- `ghostty.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `renderer.ts`, `interfaces.ts`, `search.ts` (new): find in the scrollback (ADR 055). The binding adds `setSearch`, `searchStep`, `searchSelect`, `searchState`, `searchSelectedMatch` and `searchMatches` on libghostty-vt's search (`ghostty_search_*`, with `SELECT_SCROLL` set to `NONE`: the view is webtty's own), freed with the terminal. `Terminal` adds `find`, `findNext`, `findPrevious`, `endFind`, `finding` and `onFindChange`; it steps the search in the render loop before each render, hands the renderer the matches when they changed, scrolls a selected match into view as Ghostty does (its first row at the top when none of its rows is in view), keeps a scrolled view on its rows during output while a match is selected (instead of xterm.js' scroll to the bottom; still to the bottom on the alternate screen), scrolls to the bottom on a key or a paste sent to the program as Ghostty's `scroll-to-bottom = keystroke` does (`handleInput` without a mouse report, `paste`), and sets the needle again on the engine `reset` makes. `search.ts` finds the matches over a range of rows by binary search on the newest-to-oldest list (`matchesInRows`, `highlightRows`) and holds the view arithmetic (`viewportYToShow`, `keptViewportY`). The renderer's new `setSearchHighlights` paints matches with the new theme colours `searchBackground` / `searchForeground` and the selected one with `searchSelectedBackground` / `searchSelectedForeground` (Ghostty's defaults), under the selection, and repaints a canvas row only when its matches change (`drawnSearch`, moved with the rows on a copied scroll). Upstream had no search.
- `ghostty.ts`, `types.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `interfaces.ts`, `index.ts`: desktop notifications (ADR 056). The binding installs Ghostty's `DESKTOP_NOTIFICATION` callback when the new `GhosttyTerminalConfig.desktopNotifications` is on (default true): it copies the request's `title` (`''` for OSC 9) and `body` out as UTF-8, reading only what the struct's `size` covers. `TerminalEffects` gains `notifications`, every request since `readEffects`, in order, and `DesktopNotification` is exported. `Terminal` gains the `desktopNotifications` option, passed to the engine, and `onDesktopNotification`, fired for each. Upstream ignored OSC 9 and OSC 777.
- `ghostty.ts`, `terminal.ts`, `selection-manager.ts`: OSC 133 prompt jumps and output selection (ADR 057). The binding adds `promptJumpRow` (Ghostty's viewport put on webtty's top row with `ROW`, moved with `GHOSTTY_SCROLL_VIEWPORT_DELTA_PROMPT`, read back with `GHOSTTY_TERMINAL_DATA_SCROLLBAR` and put back at the bottom; `scrollViewport` writes its value as an `isize`) and `selectOutput` (`ghostty_terminal_select_output`). `Terminal` adds `jumpToPrompt`, Ghostty's `jump_to_prompt`, scrolling the view with `scrollToLine`. A triple click with Ctrl or Cmd held selects the command's output instead of the line, as in Ghostty. Upstream had neither.
- `fn-table.ts`: not from ghostty-web. Copied unmodified (below its added header) from [gkoreli/ghostty-vt-js](https://github.com/gkoreli/ghostty-vt-js) at `248de81a188b71a1919d3c5c5bce2f99a836b5b1`, `packages/ghostty-vt-js/src/wasm/fn-table.ts`, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 ghostty-vt-js contributors ([LICENSE.ghostty-vt-js](LICENSE.ghostty-vt-js)); `bun run build` adds the notice to `dist/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES`.
- `engine/wasm-loader.ts` (from `ghostty.ts`): the wasm is read through an injected reader and fetch (`WasmLoaderDeps`; production: `Bun.file` where Bun runs, then the global `fetch`), and upstream's Node `fs/promises` fallback is removed: the browser never reached it and tests run under Bun, where `Bun.file` reads first (ADR 061). The default URL is `../../ghostty-vt/ghostty-vt-small.wasm`, for the file's new depth.
- `index.ts`: the barrel's header names its origin and its role as the only path webtty's app code imports (ADR 060, ADR 061), and it exports the webtty-original `Glide`, `AT_ONCE`, `FRAME_MS`, `linear`, `easeOutCubic`, `Pace` and `Ease` (`glide.ts`), `watchDevicePixelRatio` (`renderer.ts`) and `DisposableStore`, `listen`, `toDisposable`, `Disposable` and `ListenerTarget` (`lifecycle/disposable-store.ts`), which the app imported by deep path or did not have.

## webtty-original files

Not from upstream; each starts with, or will start with when it is next touched, `// webtty (ADR NNN), not from upstream.`

- `glide.ts`, `wheel.ts` (ADR 045), `mouse-route.ts` (ADR 051), `search.ts` (ADR 055).
- `lifecycle/disposable-store.ts` (ADR 060, ADR 065): `DisposableStore`, `listen` and `toDisposable`, the one teardown primitive of the app and, from ADR 065, of this layer.
- `engine/wasm-exports.ts`, `engine/vt-layout.ts`, `engine/official-layout.ts`, `engine/key-tables.ts`, `engine/scratch.ts` (ADR 041, ADR 042), `engine/cursor-blink.ts` (ADR 049), `engine/text-mime.ts` (ADR 052), `engine/kitty-keyboard-reply.ts` (ADR 042), `engine/key-encoder-binding.ts`, `engine/official-terminal.ts` (ADR 042, ADR 047): webtty's binding to the official wasm, moved out of `ghostty.ts` (ADR 061). Upstream's `ghostty.ts` ran the Coder wasm at fixed offsets and had none of them.

## Layout

- `lifecycle/`: teardown (`disposable-store.ts`). webtty-original.
- `input/`: keyboard and mouse input (`key-types.ts`).
- `engine/`: the binding to the official wasm: its interfaces (`cell-types.ts`, `engine-types.ts`), the export typing (`wasm-exports.ts`), the manifest reader and layout table (`vt-layout.ts`, `official-layout.ts`), the wasm loader (`wasm-loader.ts`), the key name tables (`key-tables.ts`), the scratch allocator (`scratch.ts`), the terminal (`official-terminal.ts`), the key encoder (`key-encoder-binding.ts`) and pure helpers (`cursor-blink.ts`, `text-mime.ts`, `kitty-keyboard-reply.ts`).
- `ghostty.ts`: the engine's facade: `Ghostty`, which loads the wasm and creates terminals and key encoders, and the re-exports of `engine/` its importers use.
- `link-types.ts`: the link detection contract, beside `link-detector.ts` and `providers/`.
- `types.ts`: a re-export shim for the files above until its importers move (ADR 061).

## Moves and splits

Each commit that moves code out of an upstream-derived file appends its rows here (ADR 061). The moved lines keep their `(webtty, ADR NNN)` tags, and the new file starts with `// Derived from coder/ghostty-web lib/<original>.ts (MIT, see LICENSE and PROVENANCE.md in ghostty-web/).`
